rationale: Evidence from iteration 0: all 60 development trials went off track (0 finishes). Progress was only 0.11 to 0.16, so the robot left the line within the first fraction of the course. Each trial logged one line-loss event, and max_error was about 0.06 to 0.063 m, which is right at the 0.06 m off-track limit. Steering oscillation was low (0.07 to 0.16), so the failure is drift, not jitter. Two likely causes. (1) The fixed motor mismatch in each race is a constant bias that pushes the robot to one side. With ki=0 nothing removes that steady offset, so the robot settles off-centre and eventually leaves the tape. (2) The 12 mm sensors sit on a 20 mm pitch, so a sensor sees the 25 mm tape only over a limited range of offsets. Once the robot drifts a little, the line can be lost and last_direction does not recover it. Changes: add integral action (ki=0.4) to cancel the motor-mismatch bias; enlarge sensor_size to 0.016 so each sensor sees the tape over a wider lateral range and the line is less likely to drop out; raise kp to 3.0 so the robot corrects drift faster; and raise kd to 0.3 to damp the faster correction. base_speed stays at 1.6 so this iteration isolates the steering and sensing changes. Expected result: fewer line-loss events, a lower steady offset (rms_error should drop well below 0.03), and progress past 0.5 on the oval. If the run still goes off track early, the next step is to lower base_speed. If it completes but completion_time is close to 3.0 s, raise base_speed by about 0.2. Measurements requested: per-track completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, and steering_oscillation, so I can tell whether the offset or the line loss is the limiting factor.
